newsitem.title: GERMANY: German retail sector reaches another regional deal.
newsitem.headline: German retail sector reaches another regional deal.

text.p: German retail workers and employers in the state of Hesse reached a wage accord on Tuesday night, agreeing to a 1.85 percent pay rise similar to retail deals reached in other regions, union officials said.

The agreement ensures Hesse's 175,000 shopworkers will continue to get full sick pay at least until October 1997, contrasting with other industries which face 20 percent cuts in pay during sickness from this October under new legislation.
It also provides a non-cash allowance for the planned extension of shopping hours, and a rise in the Christmas bonus. The deal will be backdated to March 1 and runs for 13 months from then.
Similar deals have been reached in Bavaria and North Rhine-Westphalia, paving the way for agreements throughout the industry comprising nearly three million workers.

The pay rise, reached late on Tuesday night in the eleventh round of talks between retail unions HBV and DAG and employers, was in line with settlements of around two percent in other industries struck earlier this year.

But the agreement to postpone the introduction of the controversial cut in sick pay from October 1 this year, introduced as part of Bonn's austerity package, puts retail workers at an advantage over employees in other sectors.

Industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG, for example, on Tuesday stepped to the forefront in implementing the cut from October 1, sparking criticism from unions and fuelling a heated debate of whether the cuts apply to existing wage contracts or only to future ones.
